recipes.title: Chicken Souvlaki with Tzatziki
recipes.dish_alt: Grilled chicken souvlaki skewers served with warm pita, tzatziki, tomatoes, and red onion
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Marinated Skewers on the Grill
recipes.prep_alt: Marinated chicken skewers grilling with golden char marks

sections.heading: Steps
items: Cut the chicken into bite-sized chunks for even cooking and easy threading onto skewers.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, crushed garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper. Toss with the chicken, cover, and marinate at least 30 minutes.
Grate the cucumber, then squeeze it hard in handfuls over the sink to wring out the water — this keeps the tzatziki thick instead of watery.
Stir the squeezed cucumber into the yogurt with the crushed garlic, dill, olive oil, and lemon juice. Taste and season, then chill until serving.
Soak wooden skewers 15 minutes if using them, then thread the marinated chicken with a little space between pieces.
Heat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high until a drop of water sizzles instantly.
Cook the skewers 3-4 minutes per side, turning every few minutes, until golden grill marks form on every side.
Check doneness by cutting into the thickest piece — it should be fully white with clear juices, no pink.
Warm the pita about 20 seconds per side in the same pan until soft and slightly puffed.
Plate warm pita, souvlaki skewers, a scoop of tzatziki, cherry tomatoes, and red onion. Finish with a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.title: Avgolemono Soup (Greek Lemon Chicken & Rice Soup)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of pale yellow avgolemono soup with shredded chicken, rice, and fresh dill
recipes.prep_alt: Hot broth being whisked in a slow stream into whisked eggs and lemon juice

sections.heading: Steps
items: Bring the chicken stock to a boil in a pot over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken breast whole and reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook 15 minutes until no longer pink in the center.
Lift the chicken out onto a plate to cool slightly, keeping the stock at a simmer.
Add the rice to the simmering stock and cook 12-15 minutes until fully tender.
Shred the cooled chicken into bite-sized pieces with two forks.
Whisk the eggs well in a heatproof bowl, then slowly whisk in the lemon juice.
Ladle about a cup of hot broth into the egg-lemon mixture in a thin stream while whisking constantly — this tempers the eggs so they don't scramble.
Lower the heat and slowly stir the warmed egg mixture back into the pot.
Add the shredded chicken back in and stir gently 1-2 minutes over low heat until pale yellow and lightly thickened. Keep it below a boil or the eggs will curdle.
Season with salt and pepper, ladle into bowls, and top with fresh dill.

recipes.title: Kotopoulo Lemonato (Greek Lemon Chicken & Potatoes)
recipes.dish_alt: Golden roasted lemon chicken thighs and potato wedges in a baking dish
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Chicken and Potatoes Tossed in Lemon Marinade
recipes.prep_alt: Raw chicken thighs and potato wedges coated in olive oil, lemon, and oregano before roasting

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, crushed garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a large baking dish.
Add the chicken thighs and potato wedges and toss until everything is well coated.
Arrange the chicken skin-side up with the potatoes spread in a single layer around it so both can brown.
Pour the stock or water around the edges of the dish, not over the chicken skin, to keep it crisp.
Roast uncovered 45-55 minutes.
Halfway through, baste the chicken and potatoes with the pan juices.
Check doneness by cutting into the thickest piece near the bone — the meat should be fully white with clear juices (165°F/74°C on a thermometer).
The potatoes are ready when a fork slides in easily and the edges look golden and crisp.
Rest 5 minutes before serving so the juices settle back into the meat.

recipes.title: Psari Plaki (Baked Lemon-Garlic Fish with Tomatoes)
recipes.dish_alt: Baked white fish fillets under a chunky tomato and vegetable sauce, garnished with parsley
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Fish Fillets Topped with Tomato Sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Fish fillets in a baking dish being covered with tomato-vegetable sauce before baking

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: White fish fillets (cod, halibut, or sea bass)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 4-5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the diced tomatoes and sliced zucchini or pepper. Simmer 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down into a chunky sauce.
Pat the fish dry, season lightly with salt and pepper, and lay it in a baking dish.
Pour the tomato-vegetable sauce over the fish and drizzle with lemon juice.
Cover tightly with foil to trap steam and keep the fish moist.
Bake covered 15 minutes, then uncover carefully and bake 5-8 minutes more.
Check doneness by pressing a fork into the thickest part — the fish should flake apart easily and look opaque, not glassy.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve straight from the baking dish with extra sauce spooned over.

recipes.title: Pastitsio (Baked Pasta with Meat Sauce & Béchamel)
recipes.dish_alt: A golden-topped square of baked pastitsio pasta bake, cut to show layers of pasta, meat sauce, and béchamel
recipes.prep_alt: Creamy béchamel sauce being whisked in a saucepan until thick and smooth

sections.heading: Steps
items: Boil the pasta 2 minutes less than the package says — it finishes cooking in the oven. Drain and set aside.
Heat the olive oil and cook the onion 4-5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and ground beef, breaking it apart as it browns, 5-6 minutes until no pink remains.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Simmer uncovered 10-15 minutes until thickened.
Melt the butter in a separate saucepan over medium-low heat, whisk in the flour, and cook 1-2 minutes until it smells toasty — this is your roux.
Slowly whisk in the milk to avoid lumps, then keep whisking over medium-low heat 5-7 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Off the heat, let the béchamel cool 2 minutes, then whisk in the egg, nutmeg, and grated cheese until smooth.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Layer half the pasta in a greased baking dish, the meat sauce, then the remaining pasta.
Spread the béchamel evenly over the top, all the way to the edges.
Bake 30-35 minutes until deep golden brown on top and bubbling at the edges.
Rest at least 15 minutes before cutting into squares so it holds together.

recipes.title: Moussaka (Layered Eggplant & Meat Bake)
recipes.dish_alt: A slice of moussaka showing layers of roasted eggplant, potato, meat sauce, and golden béchamel
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Roasting the Eggplant and Potato Slices
recipes.prep_alt: Sliced eggplant and potato rounds brushed with olive oil, arranged on a baking tray

sections.heading: Steps
items: Slice the eggplant and potato into rounds about a pencil's thickness. Salt the eggplant slices and let sit 20 minutes to pull out bitterness, then pat dry.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush both vegetables with olive oil and arrange in a single layer on baking trays.
Roast 20-25 minutes, flipping halfway, until soft and lightly golden at the edges.
Meanwhile, cook the onion in olive oil over medium heat 4-5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and ground meat, breaking it apart, and cook 5-6 minutes until no pink remains.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Simmer uncovered 10-15 minutes until thick.
Make the béchamel: melt butter, whisk in flour for a roux, whisk in milk until thickened, then cool slightly and whisk in the egg, nutmeg, and cheese.
Layer the roasted potatoes, then the eggplant, in a greased baking dish, and spread the meat sauce evenly on top.
Pour the béchamel over everything, spreading it to the edges into a smooth blanket.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 30-35 minutes until deep golden brown with bubbling edges.
Rest at least 20 minutes before cutting so the layers hold together.

recipes.title: Gemista (Rice-Stuffed Tomatoes & Peppers)
recipes.dish_alt: Rice-stuffed tomatoes and bell peppers baked until soft and lightly wrinkled
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Filling the Hollowed Vegetables with Herbed Rice
recipes.prep_alt: Hollowed tomatoes and peppers being spooned full of raw rice and herb filling

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers like lids and set aside. Scoop the flesh and seeds from the tomatoes into a bowl (save the pulp); discard the pepper seeds and ribs.
Chop the reserved tomato pulp into small pieces.
Heat the olive oil and cook the onion 4-5 minutes until soft, then the garlic 30 seconds until fragrant.

Stir in the tomato pulp, uncooked rice, parsley, mint or dill, pine nuts, sugar, salt, and pepper. Cook 2-3 minutes just to coat the rice — it stays hard here and finishes cooking inside the vegetables.
Stand the hollowed vegetables upright, snug together, in a baking dish. Spoon in the filling, only about three-quarters full so the rice has room to expand.
Replace the lids, drizzle any remaining olive oil over everything, and add a splash of water to the bottom of the dish.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 45 minutes covered.
Uncover and bake 30-45 minutes more, until the vegetables look soft and slightly wrinkled and the rice is fully tender.
Cool 10 minutes before serving — gemista is traditionally served warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Baklava (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: Golden diamond-cut squares of baklava glistening with honey syrup
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Layering Buttered Phyllo with Walnuts
recipes.prep_alt: Sheets of buttered phyllo dough being layered with a cinnamon-walnut filling

sections.heading: Steps
items: Thaw the phyllo dough per package directions. Keep the stack covered with a lightly damp towel while working, pulling one sheet at a time.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and brush a baking dish all over with melted butter.
Mix the chopped walnuts with the cinnamon.
Layer half the phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each one with melted butter before adding the next.
Sprinkle the walnut-cinnamon mixture evenly over the buttered stack.
Layer the remaining phyllo on top, buttering each sheet, finishing with a well-buttered top layer.
Cut all the way through the layers into diamond or square shapes before baking — it's much harder to cut cleanly afterward.
Bake 40-45 minutes until deep golden brown and crisp, not pale or soft.
While it bakes, simmer the sugar, water, honey, lemon juice, and cloves (if using) 5-8 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove the cloves and let the syrup cool.
Pour the cooled syrup evenly over the hot baklava as soon as it comes out of the oven — cool syrup over hot pastry keeps the layers crisp instead of soggy.
Let it sit uncovered at room temperature at least 4 hours, or overnight, before serving along the scored lines.
